provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Songs for national events
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to sing independence songs.
The pupils should be able to explain why we sing national songs.

Introduction:
We love our country Nigeria. We sing special songs on Independence Day.

Content:
Independence Day is October 1st every year. We sing songs like "Arise O Compatriots" with pride. These songs show love for Nigeria. We sing them in schools and during national events.

Class activity:
We will learn two independence songs and sing them together with our hands on our chest.

Evaluation questions:
What is Independence Day?
Name one national song.
Why do we sing national songs?

Summary:
National songs show our love for Nigeria.

topics.title: Music notation: simple notes
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify do re mi notes.
The pupils should be able to sing the scale correctly.

Introduction:
We have learned many songs. Today we learn how to read music notes.

Content:
Music notes are like letters for sounds. Do re mi fa so la ti are the seven notes. Do is the first note. We sing them in order to make the scale. Like our ABC but for music.

Class activity:
We will practice singing the do re mi scale together with clapping for each note.

Evaluation questions:
What is the first music note?
How many notes are in the scale?
Sing the scale for the class.

Summary:
The do re mi scale is the foundation of music.

topics.title: Drawing: my community
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to draw a market scene.
The pupils should be able to colour their drawing neatly.

Introduction:
We live in communities with markets and places of worship. Today we draw our community.

Content:
A community has places like markets churches and mosques. In the market we see people selling tomatoes rice and yams. We draw buildings roads and people. We use different colours to make our drawing beautiful.

Class activity:
Each pupil will draw a picture of their community showing a market and a place of worship.

Evaluation questions:
What places are in your community?
What colours do you use for the market?
Draw a simple house in your community.

Summary:
Our community has many important places we love.

topics.title: Pottery: coiling method
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to roll clay into coils.
The pupils should be able to make a small bowl using coils.

Introduction:\ Nigerians make pots from clay. Today we learn how to make pots using coils.

Content:
Clay comes from the ground. We use soft clay for pottery. The coiling method means rolling clay into long ropes. We then coil the ropes to make shapes. We can make bowls cups and plates this way.

Class activity:
Each pupil will roll clay into coils and make a small bowl by coiling the clay.

Evaluation questions:
Where does clay come from?
What is the coiling method?
What can we make with coiled clay?

Summary:
We can make beautiful pots using the coiling method.

topics.title: Tie and dye basics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to tie cloth in simple patterns.
The pupils should be able to explain the tie and dye process.

Introduction:
We see colourful clothes in the market. Many are made with tie and dye.

Content:
Tie and dye is a way to make patterns on cloth. We tie the cloth with strings or rubber bands. Then we dip it in dye. When we untie it we see patterns like dots or stripes. Adire is a famous Nigerian tie and dye cloth.

Class activity:
Each pupil will tie a small piece of cloth in a pattern and dip it in coloured water.

Evaluation questions:
What is tie and dye?
Name one pattern we can make with tie and dye.
What is Adire?

Summary:
Tie and dye makes beautiful patterns on cloth.

topics.title: Dance drama
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to perform a simple dance drama.
The pupils should be able to tell a story through dance.

Introduction:
We dance at parties and festivals. Today we dance to tell a story.

Content:
Dance drama tells stories through movement. We use our bodies faces and actions to show feelings and events. We can dance stories about animals work or celebrations. In groups we make short dance dramas.

Class activity:
Groups of pupils will create and perform a short dance drama about a market day.

Evaluation questions:
What is dance drama?
How do we tell stories in dance?
Show a happy feeling through dance.

Summary:
We can tell stories and show feelings through dance.

topics.title: Collage making
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to cut and paste pictures to make a collage.
The pupils should be able to tell a story using a collage.

Introduction:
We have made drawings. Today we make pictures from other pictures.

Content:
A collage is a picture made from many small pictures or papers. We cut pictures from old magazines or papers. Then we paste them on paper to make a new picture. We can make collages about animals families or our community.

Class activity:
Each pupil will make a collage showing their family by cutting and pasting pictures.

Evaluation questions:
What is a collage?
What materials do we need for collage?
What story does your collage tell?

Summary:
Collages are made from many pictures to tell a story.

topics.title: Poster design
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to design a poster with letters and pictures.
The pupils should be able to write a simple message on a poster.

Introduction:
We see posters in school and on the street. They give us information.

Content:
Posters have big letters and pictures to catch our eyes. They tell us important things like "Keep the school clean" or "Read books every day". We use bright colours and simple words. We can make posters for our classroom.

Class activity:
Each pupil will design a poster with the message "Keep the school clean" with pictures and letters.

Evaluation questions:
What is a poster?
Why do we use big letters on posters?
What message is on your poster?

Summary:
Posters give us important information with pictures and words.

topics.title: Class exhibition
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to arrange their art works neatly.
The pupils should be able to explain their art to others.

Introduction:
We have made many beautiful things. Today we show them to the class.

Content:
An exhibition is when we show our art works. We arrange them nicely on tables or boards. We can explain what we made and how we made it. Everyone can see our drawings pottery and collages.

Class activity:
Each pupil will put one of their art works on display and explain it to the class.

Evaluation questions:
What is an exhibition?
How do we arrange art works?
Explain what you made for the exhibition.

Summary:
We show our art works and tell others about them.

topics.title: Revision and assessment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recall what we learned this year.
The pupils should be able to show their best art work.

Introduction:
We have learned many things in Cultural and Creative Arts. Today we remember them all.

Content:
We learned songs music notation drawing pottery tie and dye dance drama collage and posters. We made many beautiful things. We will show our best work and talk about what we learned.

Class activity:
Each pupil will bring their best art work and tell the class what they learned this year.

Evaluation questions:
What did you learn in Cultural and Creative Arts?
Show your favourite art work.
What was the most fun activity for you?

Summary:
We remember all we learned and show our best art works.
